**Monday, November 16, 2026 - **

_**Iran:** Iran claims six-drone strike on U.S. radar system in Bahrain. U.S.
deploys third aircraft carrier to Middle East. Six oil tankers struck mines,
caught fire in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says. IRGC claims capture of eighth
intact U.S. drone in Hormuz. Israel reportedly warns U.S. of Iranian drone
plot targeting President Donald Trump; Tehran denounces "disinformation."
Bahrain sentences convicts 69 defendants over alleged ties to Iran,
confiscates $21.2 million._

_**Palestine:** Israeli forces kill one Palestinian, wound five others across
Gaza. Israeli forces detain 13 Palestinians in occupied West Bank raids.
Palestinian prisoners suffer severe weight loss and scabies in Israeli prison.
Australia, Canada, UK, and Italy demand Israel allow 150,000 tents into Gaza
amid deadly winter storms. Guardian: Israeli uploaded millions of photos of
Palestinians to Amazon's facial recognition platform. Palestinian lawmaker
elected deputy speaker of Israeli Knesset._

_**Yemen:** Ansarallah seizes over 2,000 square kilometers in southern Yemen,
takes control of Bab al-Mandab front. Three Yemenis, including child, killed
in strikes on Sana'a and Amran. Ansarallah claims strikes on Riyadh airport,
financial center, and Saudi oil pipeline. Ansarallah releases 600 detainees in
Sana'a, bringing unilateral releases to 2,612. Armed men approach oil tanker
east of Yemen's Socotra island._

_**Lebanon:** Israeli forces abduct two Lebanese brothers in Shebaa, strike
southern Lebanon despite ceasefire. Israel strikes Syria-Lebanon border,
claims weapons shipment destined for Hezbollah._

_**U.S.:** Van Hollen accuses Schumer of attempting to rush Senate election.
Senate permitting reform, energy bill headed for final passage. U.S. loses
measles elimination status. Alaska continues counting votes, with Peltola
increasing her lead over Sullivan. Trump's portfolio likely held $13 million
to $62 million in Nvidia stock as of August, the Washington Post finds.
International student enrollment falls at U.S. colleges. Incoming Rep. Don
Leonard backing Ayanna Pressley. Federal prosecutor accuses Warren of
preparing "to target private individuals close to" Trump and orders her to
preserve documents. Transportation Sec. Duffy declines to apologize for
Friday's nationwide ground stop._

_**International:** UAE remains major hub for gold smuggled from war zones
despite new regulations. Saudi Arabia executes two men. Imran Khan details
inhumane treatment, asks for urgent medical care in letter to justices. About
4.5 million people have returned to Sudan, UNHCR says. Africa CDC says the
Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is still not under control.
Somaliland's intelligence agency says it briefly detained five U.S. nationals
it accused of threatening national security. Ecuador's President Noboa denies
the U.S. has a military base near Guayaquil. Guatemala decrees a 30-day state
of emergency in its eastern provinces after lawmakers killed. Mexican
journalist found dead in Guerrero. Martine Moise, widow of Haiti's
assassinated president Jovenel Moise, registers as a presidential candidate._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **Iran claims six-drone strike on U.S. radar system in Bahrain:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [said](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/249407/Iran-targets-US-air-defense-at-Bahrain-s-Al-Rifaa-base-IRGC) Sunday that it launched six drones successfully targeting a U.S. air defense radar system at Bahrain's Al-Rifaa helicopter base, describing the operation as the second phase of its response to U.S. military actions in the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain's military, however, said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed the Iranian attacks before they reached their targets.

    * The strikes followed an earlier Iranian drone attack on Bahrain on Friday, the first targeting a Gulf country since September, when the IRGC also claimed to have destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar system.

  * **U.S. deploys third aircraft carrier to Middle East:** The United States deployed a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East amid heightened tensions with Iran. The USS Theodore Roosevelt entered the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility on Sunday, joining the USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush.

    * Meanwhile, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency extended its warnings for airlines operating in Middle Eastern airspace until January 31, citing continued risks from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The advisory covers Iran, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Lebanon, Iraq, and the wider Gulf region.

  * **Six oil tankers struck mines, caught fire in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says:** Iran's IRGC Navy [claimed](https://en.irna.ir/news/86322979/Two-more-tankers-hit-naval-mines-in-Strait-of-Hormuz-says-IRGC) Monday that two more oil tankers struck naval mines overnight while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz through a "prohibited" southern route, triggering explosions and fires. The IRGC claimed the vessels were operating under U.S. military guidance, bringing the number of tankers it claims to have sunk since Sunday to six.

    * Iran's regular navy reported that another tanker caught fire after striking a mine east of the strait. The reports have not been independently verified.

    * Separately, UK Maritime Trade Operations reported Monday that a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz, sparking a fire in its engine room. All crew members were accounted for, while the extent of the damage and environmental impact remain unknown.

  * **IRGC claims capture of eighth intact U.S. drone in Hormuz:** The IRGC Navy [said](https://en.irna.ir/news/86323487/US-drone-captured-intact-IRGC-Navy) Monday that it forced a U.S. MQM-170 drone to land intact using electronic warfare systems in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said it was the fourth MQM-170 and the eighth U.S. drone captured intact by its forces in the strait. The force also claimed to have intercepted, captured, or destroyed several other types of U.S. drones, including MQ-9s, MQ-1s, and LUCAS attack drones, since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

  * **Israel reportedly warns U.S. of Iranian drone plot targeting Trump; Tehran denounces "disinformation": **Israel's Mossad intelligence agency provided the CIA with information suggesting Iran was planning drone attacks targeting President Donald Trump and senior administration officials, Israel Hayom reported Saturday. The newspaper said the warnings prompted heightened security in Washington, including the relocation of some officials to protected facilities and a reduction in Trump's public appearances.

    * Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said U.S. officials receive "aspirational threats from Iran" daily, adding that Washington was already aware of the threats and was prepared to respond.

    * Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejected the allegations, accusing Israel of orchestrating a disinformation campaign to build Western public support for escalating the war. "Fear must be manufactured to push the public into backing an escalation of the war," he said.

  * **Bahrain sentences convicts 69 defendants over alleged ties to Iran, confiscates $21.2 million:** A Bahraini court on Monday [sentenced](https://birdbh.org/2026/11/bahrain-sentences-64-defendants-to-life-imprisonment-and-five-to-15-years-in-mass-trial-of-shia-clerics-amid-allegations-of-torture-and-coerced-confessions/) 64 defendants to life imprisonment and five others to 15 years in prison over accusations of establishing a group linked to Iran's IRGC and seeking to overthrow the government, according to the Britain-based Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy. Bahrain's public prosecution [said](https://aa.com.tr/ar/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A3%D8%AD%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D8%AC%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A4%D8%A8%D8%AF-%D9%8815-%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%A8%D9%82%D8%B6%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%A8%D8%B7%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%B1%D8%B3-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AB%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A/4126484) the court also ordered the confiscation of more than $21.2 million and imposed fines of approximately $265,000 on some defendants.

# Palestine

  * **Israeli forces kill one Palestinian, wound five others across Gaza:** A young Palestinian man was [shot and killed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/16/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B5-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%AC%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A7) by Israeli forces in the Al-Qassasib neighborhood of Jabalia, northern Gaza, on Monday, according to WAFA. Two other Palestinians sustained gunshot wounds in the nearby town of Beit Lahia.

    * In southern Gaza, Israeli forces shot and wounded three Palestinians, including a child, inside a school south of Khan Younis.

  * **Israeli forces detain 13 Palestinians in occupied West Bank raids:**

    * **Hebron:** Israeli forces [detained](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/16/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AE%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-11-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%8A%D8%B1) 11 Palestinians, including journalist Yasser Jaradat, during a raid on Sa'ir, on Monday, according to WAFA. In nearby Al-Shuyukh, soldiers closed the town's entrance, seized vehicles, and turned homes into military posts. Schools in both towns suspended classes due to the military presence.

    * **Jenin:** Israeli forces [detained](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/16/%D8%AC%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%8A%D9%82%D8%AA%D8%AD%D9%85) two Palestinians after raiding their homes in Jenin city. Soldiers also raided Al-Fandaqumiya, Burqin, and Rummana, firing tear gas in the latter and causing several cases of suffocation. On Sunday, an Israeli military jeep ran over two Palestinians riding a motorcycle east of Jenin, leaving one with a broken foot and the other with a head injury, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society.

    * **Nablus:** Israeli forces raided Beit Furik, east of Nablus, and Beita, south of the city. In Beit Furik, soldiers stormed several businesses, destroyed equipment in one shop, and assaulted residents, according to WAFA. In Beita, Israeli forces entered Palestinian homes and fired live ammunition and tear gas canisters.

    * **Tubas:** Israeli settlers [fired](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/16/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%B7%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B1%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B4%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%82-%D8%B7%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B3) live ammunition toward Palestinian herders in northern Yarza, east of Tubas, forcing them to abandon grazing areas.

  * **Palestinian prisoners suffer severe weight loss and scabies in Israeli prison:** Palestinian prisoners held at Israel's Naqab Prison are suffering deteriorating health conditions amid medical neglect, poor sanitation, and a lack of treatment, the Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs reported Monday. Mustafa Abu Al-Fiya, 39, from Tulkarm, suffers from spinal disc problems and heart disease and has lost approximately 14 kilograms without receiving necessary medical care. Qais Al-Habal, 25, from west of Ramallah, has lost 39 kilograms, and suffers from severe scabies and boils. Two other prisoners from Jerusalem are also suffering from scabies.

  * **Australia, Canada, UK, and Italy urge Israel to allow 150,000 tents into Gaza amid deadly winter storms:** The foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, the UK, and Italy [issued](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/joint-foreign-ministers-statement-on-gaza--2) a joint statement Monday urging Israel to immediately allow 150,000 tents and other essential supplies held at the border into Gaza, warning that the humanitarian situation is "dire" as winter storms devastate displacement camps. "The crossings must be opened, and the tents allowed in," the ministers said without threatening any repercussions or sanctions, calling for "immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access." Recent flooding has damaged or submerged tens of thousands of tents, while at least four children and a woman have been killed.

  * **Guardian: Israel uploaded millions of photos of Palestinians to Amazon 's facial recognition platform:** The Israeli military uploaded 3.5 million photos to Amazon's cloud platform in order to use the company's facial recognition technology to analyze images of Palestinians, according to an [exclusive report](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/israel-amazon-facial-recognition-palestinians) by the Guardian.

    * The vast catalogue of images was moved into Amazon's cloud in the early months of the Israeli genocide in Gaza that began in October 2023. The large set of images was moved into an Amazon data center near Tel Aviv.

    * The Israeli military informed Amazon of the decision to upload the images in early 2024 so it could use Rekognition, Amazon's AI-powered image analysis platform.

    * An Israeli military source told the Guardian that Amazon's cloud infrastructure was used due to the "very large scale" of images collected at checkpoints in Gaza that Palestinians were made to pass through after being forcibly displaced by the Israeli assault.

  * **Palestinian lawmaker elected deputy speaker of Israeli Knesset:** Ahmed Tibi, chairman of the Joint List faction and leader of the Ta'al Party, has been elected deputy speaker of Israel's parliament, the Knesset. His appointment follows historic gains by parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel in last month's elections, with the Joint List and United Arab List (Ra'am) securing a combined 19 seats.

# Yemen

  * **Ansarallah seizes over 2,000 square kilometers in southern Yemen, takes control of Bab al-Mandab front:** Ansarallah [captured](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2122093057134796933?a=tqsE8W-29hzj8K8JtTw&s=46) over 2,000 square kilometers of the Al-Madaribah Wa Ras Al-Arah district of the Lahij governorate in a single day with its forces now controlling all of the Bab Al-Mandab front.

    * The Ansarallah offensive in Lahij Governorate in southern Yemen effectively encircled the remaining forces loyal to the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council in the Bab al-Mandab area on Sunday.

    * Ansarallah forces reached Al-Kharaz camp at the southern foot of Jabal Kharaz in the Al-Madaribah Wa Ras Al-Arah district and established fire control over the last remaining road out of Bab al-Mandab.

    * Saudi-backed forces said they are withdrawing from positions overlooking the strait to reinforce defenses around their interim capital, Aden.

    * The UN Refugee Agency warned that fighting is approaching a displacement camp housing 9,600 people in Lahij governorate.

  * **Three Yemenis, including child, killed in strikes on Sana 'a and Amran: **Three Yemenis, including a child, were killed and 15 others wounded in separate strikes on Ansarallah-controlled areas of Yemen on Monday, according to the Associated Press citing health authorities. A drone strike on a home in the Al-Sarar neighborhood of Sana'a killed a child and wounded seven people, while airstrikes on a privately owned fuel station in Harf Sufian district of Amran governorate killed two people and wounded eight others. Ansarallah blamed Saudi Arabia for the attacks.

  * **Ansarallah claims strikes on Riyadh airport, financial center, and Saudi oil pipeline:** Ansarallah [launched](https://x.com/yah_saree/status/2122025225902797088?a=q904NliTY3VO-yJEIoo&s=46) two ballistic missiles targeting King Khalid International Airport and a financial center in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, military spokesperson Yahya Saree said Sunday. Saree also claimed that two drones struck pumping stations 5 and 6 along Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline in the Riyadh region. He said both operations successfully hit their targets. The claims have not been independently verified.

  * **Ansarallah releases 600 detainees in Sana 'a, bringing unilateral releases to 2,612: **Ansarallah [unilaterally released](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/yemen-s-houthis-unilaterally-release-600-detainees-red-cross/4125877) 600 detainees in the capital, Sana'a, on Sunday, according to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The organization said its delegates interviewed detainees privately before their release and provided assistance for their return home, but did not participate in selecting those freed. Abdul Qader al-Murtada, head of Ansarallah's National Committee for Prisoners' Affairs, said the latest release brought the total number of detainees unilaterally freed by the group since the war began to 2,612. Last month, the ICRC reported that Ansarallah had released another 159 detainees.

  * **Armed men approach oil tanker east of Yemen 's Socotra island: **A tanker was approached by a suspicious ship and a small boat carrying four armed men approximately 430 nautical miles east of Yemen's Socotra island, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported Monday. The tanker's captain reported seeing a ladder aboard the smaller vessel during the incident.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli forces abduct two Lebanese brothers in Shebaa, strike southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:** Israeli forces advanced into the outskirts of Shebaa in southern Lebanon on Monday, raided a home, and [abducted](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/574392/%D9%82%D9%88%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D8%AE%D8%AA%D8%B7%D9%81%D8%AA-%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%B4%D9%82%D9%8A%D9%82%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AE%D9%84-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B2%D9%84%D9%87%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%B9%D9%86%D8%AF-%D8%A3%D8%B7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%81-%D8%B4%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%A7-2) two brothers, before withdrawing, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The Khiam Rehabilitation Center for Victims of Torture condemned the abductions, noting that a third brother, Maher, was abducted by Israeli forces in June 2025 while herding goats near the town.

    * Elsewhere, Israeli warplanes [struck](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/574456/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D9%83%D9%81%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%A8%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%AA-14) Kfartabnit in the Nabatieh district, while intermittent artillery shelling targeted the Ain Al-Samahiyah area between Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Mifdoun.

    * Two Israeli drones also exploded over the Al-Rajm area of Mifdoun within 15 minutes of each other.

  * **Israel strikes Syria-Lebanon border, claims weapons shipment destined for Hezbollah:** The Israeli military [said](https://x.com/idf/status/2122251733258662196?a=9bcZ74595iw1jsYamuo&s=46) Monday that it struck a weapons shipment allegedly destined for Hezbollah along the Syria-Lebanon border, accusing the Lebanese group of using areas across Lebanon for weapons smuggling and military activities. Israel said it would continue operations to "remove threats."

# U.S. News

  * **Van Hollen accuses Schumer of attempting to rush Senate election:** Sen. **Chris Van Hollen** , the Maryland senator challenging Schumer for the job of majority leader, charged New York's Sen. **Chuck Schumer** with pushing for a "coronation," but told Politico he had the support to block any attempt to move the election to this week. Schumer's camp denied any such plan exists, emphasizing his confidence that he retains at least majority support inside the caucus and will be re-elected leader.

    * Van Hollen**** addressed his challenge to Schumer on ABC's "This Week" on Sunday, saying that he thinks he has "a very open lane" in the race, and accusing Schumer's team of spreading "misinformation" and trying to "instill fear" in senators who may back him. He argued that midterm voters rejected Trump's policies, wars, corruption, and costs but "haven't fully hired the Democrats," so "going back to business as usual and status quo" won't earn their trust. Schumer has said he has the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader.

  * **Senate permitting reform, energy bill headed for final passage:** The so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is undergoing final negotiations as environmental lawyers push to add ways to challenge energy projects and tribal advocates look to tighten tribal participation provisions. The clean energy industry remains in lockstep support of the bill, as does the fossil fuel industry.

  * **U.S. loses measles elimination status:** The U.S. [lost](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/14/us-loses-measles-elimination-status) its measles elimination status, an expert panel from the Pan American Health Organization announced last week. The organization made the widely expected decision after a three-day meeting in Washington, concluding the virus has been transmitted continuously for more than 12 months. The CDC counts 5,412 confirmed cases this year versus 2,289 in all of 2025, the highest since 1991's 9,643, with Pennsylvania's outbreak accounting for more than 1,500 cases and six deaths. These are likely undercounts. Vaccine skepticism accounts for much of this rise, with distrust in vaccines fueled by ranking officials, including Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Canada and the UK have also lost their status over the past year.

  * **Alaska continues counting votes, with Peltola increasing her lead over Sullivan:** Democrat **Mary Peltola** now [leads](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-11-13/alaska-elects-democrat-jonathan-kreiss-tomkins-governor) in Alaska's Senate contest by nearly 4 points, more than 11,000 votes, after the latest batch of votes was counted and results were released on Saturday. She netted nearly 2,000 votes from the latest batch. Decision Desk HQ shows her at 49.8% with 91% counted, just shy of the majority she needs to avoid ranked-choice tabulation. Her campaign again declared victory, saying "there is no mathematical path for Sullivan to win," though no major outlet has called the race as of Monday. All votes must be reported by Nov. 18.

    * Democrat **Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins** won the state's gubernatorial race, with the AP calling the race in his favor on Friday. Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, will replace Republican **Mike Dunleavy** , who is term-limited and has held the post since 2018. He described himself as a "man of the middle" who would work in a "bipartisan" fashion during the campaign and said he would pay special attention to "unsexy and non-glamorous" issues like wait times for state permits and government benefits like Medicaid. He will be the state's first Democratic governor since 2002.

  * **Trump 's portfolio likely held $13 million to $62 million in Nvidia stock as of August, the Washington Post finds: **President Donald Trump, whose portfolio has logged tens of thousands of stock trades in his second term, [held](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/11/16/trumps-stake-nvidia-grew-much-62-million-before-scandal-broke-out/) between $13 and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August, according to a review of his financial disclosures from that month. The actual value range may have been higher, the Post noted, citing Nvidia's rising share price. During his second administration, Trump has given the company's leadership major concessions, allowing its former CEO **Jensen Huang** extraordinary access to his administration. The White House maintains that "the President does not pick or trade individual stocks" and that independent managers handle his portfolio. Nvidia reportedly donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom, which it says was "independent of business interests."

  * **International student enrollment falls at U.S. colleges** : New international student enrollment at U.S. universities [fell](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/international-student-college-enrollment-declines.html) 15% this fall after an 18% drop last year, according to a survey of more than 800 universities released by The Institute of International Education on Monday. The survey shows that total international enrollment is down 9%, following a 3% drop last year. The administration's trade war with China and immigration crackdown are likely causes for this decline, as are the budget cuts at major research universities. 

  * **Incoming Rep. Don Leonard backing Ayanna Pressley:** Ohio's **Don Leonard** , who made headlines by saying that he had been threatened by senior Democrats over his reluctance to back Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, appeared on Breaking Points Monday morning and said that he was leaning toward voting for **Ayanna Pressley** , who has not announced a campaign but has been drawing support regardless. The leadership election is scheduled for Wednesday, and Jeffries still has no official opponent.

  * **Federal prosecutor accuses Warren of preparing "to target private individuals close to" Trump and orders her to preserve documents: **U.S**.** Attorney for the Southern District of Texas **Aaron Reitz** , a former chief of staff to Sen. **Ted Cruz**(R-Texas), [wrote](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/15/federal-prosecutor-elizabeth-warren-oversight-01166765) Sunday that Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee, appears "eager to wield" the gavel "like a tomahawk, hunting for the scalps of President Trump's private associates," one of several barbed references made to Native Americans made in the letter, alluding to attacks made on Warren over her past claims of Native ancestry. He gave "formal notice" to preserve documents on oversight efforts, warning of "sanctions, adverse-inference instructions, or other penalties," and said he asked the same of Sens. **Richard Blumenthal** (D-Conn.) and **Elissa Slotkin**(D-Mich.).

  * **Duffy declines to apologize for Friday 's nationwide ground stop: **A router being [repaired](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/15/sean-duffy-air-travel-outage-01166655) by an FAA contractor in Arkansas overwhelmed the nation's aviation communication network, leading the agency to ground all flights on Friday. The delay stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers and caused thousands of cancellations through the weekend. Transportation Secretary**Sean Duffy** told NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday that Friday's nationwide ground stop "happened on my watch," but "I can't apologize for what was passed off to us." He told the program that operations should normalize by Monday, but that he can't guarantee it won't recur until an investigation is completed.

# Other International News

  * **UAE remains major hub for gold smuggled from war zones despite new regulations** : The United Arab Emirates (UAE) remains a key trading hub for gold smuggled from war zones despite new regulations introduced by the Emirati government under international pressure, according to a new [report](https://www.swissaid.ch/en/articles/illicit-gold-continues-to-flow-into-dubai-on-a-massive-scale/) by Swissaid.

    * At least 591 tons of such illicit gold valued at $74 billion was imported into the UAE, mostly in 2024, the report found.

    * Much of the smuggled gold was conflict-related and smuggled out of Africa--including Guinea, Mali, and Sudan--as well as other countries including Russia and Yemen.

    * "The UAE remains by far the main destination for gold linked to armed conflicts in Africa. And it continues to be a major destination for gold exports from countries subject to international sanctions," the report said.

    * Switzerland was the leading importer of gold from the UAE and does not appear to be scaling back its trade with Dubai. Between January and September 2026, more than 400 tons of Emirati gold were imported into Switzerland.
